_sourcePolicy.preference: Russian / Soviet primary sources first (ROSFOND-2010 evaluated nuclear data, NIKIET and RRC-Kurchatov design documentation, the plant technical description). Western and IAEA documents are used only where no Russian primary source covers the quantity, and are labelled as such.
_sourcePolicy.why: Ben's standing instruction: the designers of the RBMK are the best-placed source for its data. A quantity sourced from INSAG-7 or NUREG-1250 is a second-best fallback, not a first choice, and must be marked so that it can be replaced when a Russian source is found.
_sourcePolicy.applies_to: Every entry in this register. A nuclear-data quantity should ultimately come from ROSFOND-2010, not ENDF/B-VIII.0.

_comment: Registry of the numeric constants the RBMK model rests on, with their source. Mission rule 2: nothing is guessed. status is one of: verified (cites a primary source, with sourceUrl + quote), to_verify (a reference value not yet confirmed against a primary source), placeholder (a value with no source at all, allowed only as a FALLBACK that is unused while real data is present). The build gate warns on to_verify and FAILS on any non-fallback placeholder; the self-test additionally requires every verified entry to carry a sourceUrl and a quote.

INSAG-7.title: IAEA Safety Series No. 75-INSAG-7, The Chernobyl Accident: Updating of INSAG-1

NUREG-1250.title: Report on the Accident at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Station (NUREG-1250), US Nuclear Regulatory Commission, January 1987
NUREG-1250.publisher: US Nuclear Regulatory Commission (with DOE, EPRI, EPA, FEMA, INPO)
NUREG-1250.note: Independent of IAEA/INSAG. Its Table 2.4 (section 2.3.2) is compiled from Soviet primary sources (Dollezhal 1980a, USSR 1986, Romanenko 1982, Virgil'ev 1979). Used here to CORROBORATE the feedback-coefficient signs, not as the value source.

OpenMC.title: OpenMC 0.16.0 Monte Carlo neutron transport (computed in this repo), ENDF/B-VIII.0 cross-sections
OpenMC.note: Not a document but an independent COMPUTATION: a first-principles lattice-cell model of an RBMK fuel channel (openmc/rbmk_cell.py, openmc/rbmk_void_coeff.py). No tabulated coefficient is fed in — the void coefficient is derived from cross-section data plus graphite S(a,b). It yields +0.035 dk/k per unit void at the operating point (simple dk/k). An earlier version gave +0.015 and appeared to corroborate INSAG-7 (+0.02); that agreement was an artefact of two channel-geometry errors (an 80 mm bore instead of 88 mm, and fuel/water volume fractions of 0.62/0.26 instead of the true 0.324/0.570) and is WITHDRAWN. See docs/VOID-COEFF-ROOT-CAUSE.md.

SUZ-CARTOGRAM.title: SUZ control-panel cartogram of ChNPP Unit 4 (RBMK_Reactor_ChNPP-4.svg)
SUZ-CARTOGRAM.publisher: Wikimedia Commons (drawn from the unit's SUZ panel); legend confirmed against the Nucleopedia SUZ panel table and the units 3/4 operating regulation §2.11.6
SUZ-CARTOGRAM.note: The SVG carries 1,884 rect elements, one per channel, with an explicit fill per rod type. Decoded geometry is committed as rbmk_cartogram_ch4.json. Counts reproduce exactly: AZ 24, PK-AZ 24, AR 12, USP 24, RR 127, DKE 12, TK 1,661 = 1,872 channels.

SUZ-PANEL-TABLE.title: Nucleopedia: Benutzer:TZV/Reaktorunfall — Steuer- und Kontrollsystem table
SUZ-PANEL-TABLE.publisher: Nucleopedia (de), accessed via the Wayback Machine snapshot of 2022-11-01
SUZ-PANEL-TABLE.note: Per-type absorber length, displacer length, insertion time, scram time and reactivity worth for units 3 and 4. The live site is Cloudflare-protected; the archived copy is readable.

DOE-NE-0076.title: Report of the U.S. Department of Energy's Team Analyses of the Chernobyl-4 Atomic Energy Station Accident Sequence, DOE/NE-0076
DOE-NE-0076.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Assistant Secretary for Nuclear Energy, November 1986
DOE-NE-0076.note: Independent US government engineering assessment. Appendix G, Table G-2 'Control Rod Specifications' is a dimensioned table of the actual pre-1986 rod, and is the only source found that states the rod DIAMETERS at all. Used because no Russian primary source for the rod diameters has yet been obtained; labelled Western and replaceable.

delayed.beta_eff.source: RBMK literature (value commonly quoted for the RBMK-1000). INSAG-7 uses beta_eff as the reactivity unit but does not tabulate its numeric value.
delayed.beta_eff.note: To confirm against a NIKIET/design source. The RBMK used its own six-group delayed-neutron set (see delayed.lambda_i).

delayed.generation_time.note: To confirm against a NIKIET/design source.

delayed.lambda_i.note: The RBMK used its own six-group set — replace from a NIKIET/ABBN source. INSAG-7 Annex II notes the accident analyses used 18 delayed-neutron groups, so a higher-group RBMK set exists.

delayed.beta_fractions.note: RBMK-specific group abundances to be sourced (see delayed.lambda_i).

feedback.void_coeff.source: INSAG-7 Table II-I (p. 105), 'Void coefficient of reactivity at the working point' = +2.0e-4 per % void; +2.0e-4 per 1% = 0.020 per unit void fraction. INSAG-7 sec. 2.1 gives the full range: -1.3e-4 (fresh fuel) to +(2.0-2.5)e-4 per % void (steady-state refuelling).
feedback.void_coeff.quote: Void coefficient of reactivity af at the working point (%-' (5k/k) void) +2.0 x 10"4
feedback.void_coeff.corroboration: OpenMC lattice-cell Monte Carlo (openmc/, ENDF/B-VIII.0) gives +0.035 dk/k per unit void at the operating point (simple dk/k), with the channel geometry corrected, independently — same sign as the +0.02 above but ~1.75x larger (a single-channel infinite lattice overstates the whole-core operating coefficient). The earlier +0.015 'agreement' is WITHDRAWN: it came from a channel-geometry error. Minecraft displays this result via /rbmk openmc (OpenMcResult.java).

feedback.doppler_coeff.source: INSAG-7 Table II-I (p. 105), 'Fuel temperature coefficient of reactivity' = -1.2e-5 per degC.
feedback.doppler_coeff.quote: Fuel temperature coefficient of reactivity aT ("C"1) -1.2 x 10'5

feedback.graphite_coeff.source: INSAG-7 Table II-I (p. 105) states the graphite temperature coefficient as +6e-5 (POSITIVE), and INSAG-7 sec. 4.7.3 twice calls it 'the positive graphite temperature coefficient of reactivity'. INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED: NUREG-1250 (US NRC, Jan 1987) sec. 2.3.2.2 states 'The graphite temperature coefficient is positive', and its Table 2.4 gives +3.2e-5 (fresh) to +6e-5 (steady-state) per degC.
feedback.graphite_coeff.note: RESOLVED (2026-11-18): the sign conflict is closed -- the code now carries the POSITIVE value, as both sources require. The live core applies it through the cross sections: RbmkGraphiteTemp scales the homogenised cell constants by the thermal-scattering temperature dependence derived from the OpenMC cell (openmc/rbmk_graphite_mgxs.py), so the effect enters the neutron balance. Magnitude of the derived per-constant slopes is to_verify (chord slope 600-800 K extrapolated to the 873 K operating point); the whole-core value here is the sourced +6e-5.
feedback.graphite_coeff.quote: Graphite temperature coefficient of reactivity ac (CC~') 6 x 10~5

feedback.power_coeff.source: Lumped damping term in the model. NOT the INSAG-7 'fast power coefficient' (-0.5e-4 dk/k per MW(th), Table II-I): that is per MW and gives ~-0.16 dk/k at 3200 MW(th), a different quantity in different units. The model's per-unit-power coefficient still needs a source.
feedback.power_coeff.note: Confirm the intended definition (per unit power fraction vs per MW) and source the value.

xenon.coeff.source: Reference value; INSAG-7 does not tabulate a xenon worth.
xenon.coeff.note: To confirm against a NIKIET/design source. (Note: Xenon.java uses a -0.03 equilibrium scale, and ReactorCore/SpatialReactorCore hard-code 0.024 separately — these should be reconciled to one sourced value.)

rodworth.scale.source: Reference worth used to scale the perturbation sum. INSAG-7 Table II-I gives per-rod efficiencies instead: 'Minimum efficiency of RCPS rods 10.5%' and 'Efficiency of manual control rods 7.5%' (of the core's reactivity), plus rod travel speed 0.4 m/s (Annex II).
rodworth.scale.note: Replace with a measured/design rod-worth curve. The INSAG-7 efficiencies (10.5% / 7.5%) are the calibration target.

spatial.void_feedback.unit: dk/k per unit void (measured from the 3D solver)
spatial.void_feedback.source: Measured from RbmkSolver3D: dk/d(void) = +0.105/unit, i.e. ~5x the INSAG-7 value (+0.020/unit). The derived one-node lattice cell overstates the feedback; the calibration the legacy path applied (VOID_FEEDBACK_SCALE) was removed when the derived constants were wired in (commit ebaab1c).
spatial.void_feedback.note: This is why SpatialReactorCoreSelfTest's AZ-5 check ('the core is shut down after AZ-5') FAILS: after a scram the fuel cooldown contributes ~+0.039 dk/k of positive reactivity (Doppler also ~7x strong), cancelling the ~0.038 dk/k rod worth. The spatial feedbacks must be re-anchored to INSAG-7 before the spatial core can be called correct.

xsec.void_feedback_scale.source: Hand-set scale used only by the legacy fallback cell when the derived lattice table is missing. Not used when rbmk_lattice.json is present.

xsec.doppler_feedback_scale.source: Hand-set scale used only by the legacy fallback cell. Not used when the derived lattice table is present.

lattice.library.source: Russian national evaluated nuclear data library, evaluated at IPPE (Nikolaev et al.) - the NIKIET/Russian lineage the design was computed with. Imported as ENDF-6, resonances reconstructed with NJOY RECONR/BROADR, reduced to the 2-group cell by tools/lattice/emit_constants.py --source rosfond.
lattice.library.note: Replaces ENDF/B-VIII.0 (openmc mirror), which was the to_verify placeholder. k_water 1.28245, k_void 1.40145, rho +0.06621 dk/k = +10.19 beta. Re-emitted 2026-11-18 after the pressure-tube bore was corrected from 88 mm (mislabelled inner) to 80 mm (88 mm OD, 4 mm wall, per INSAG-7 and Russian tube notation); the old 1.28932 was the same code on the wrong bore. The shipped rbmk_lattice.json carries library=ROSFOND-2010 and libraryStatus=verified; LatticeTableSelfTest now FAILS if the library is not ROSFOND, so a fallback to a Western library cannot pass silently. The citation is the ENDF-6 head record of the data files themselves (MF=1/MT=451), which names the evaluation: '92-U -235  IPPE  EVAL-OCT05 NIKOLAEV M.N.' and '----RUSFOND  MATERIAL 9235'. The IAEA portal that distributes ROSFOND returns HTTP 403 to this sandbox, so the archive was supplied locally and imported from tools/lattice/rosfond_raw; the URL is the distribution point, the quote is the provenance.

decayheat.equilibrium.source: Way-Wigner decay-heat law H(t)/P0 = 0.066 t^-0.2 for long operation (standard thermal-reactor value; see Glasstone & Sesonske). The 6.5% equilibrium figure is the value at shutdown after long operation.
decayheat.equilibrium.note: The group constants (lambda_i, c_i) in DecayHeat.java are a least-squares fit of this curve over 1 s..1 day, with sum(c_i) fixed to this value. To confirm the 6.5% figure against a NIKIET/SKALA source.

xsec.void_worth_scale.source: Calibration: the derived lattice cell's whole-core void worth (drho/dvoid = +0.0810 at the working point, dial 1.0) is 4x the sourced INSAG-7 working-point value (+0.020). The derived cell is blended toward its zero-void state by this factor so the whole-core void coefficient matches INSAG-7. The SHAPE of the void dependence stays the derived physics; only its magnitude is set to the source.
xsec.void_worth_scale.measured: +0.0227 drho/dvoid at the working point with the dial at 0.233 (dial 1.0 gives +0.0810). Re-measured 2026-11-18 on the ROSFOND lattice with RbmkSolver3D at nominal rod insertion.
xsec.void_worth_scale.note: THIS IS AN INSAG-7 ANCHOR, and INSAG-7 is rank 4 in Ben's trust hierarchy. Removing it is the 'method change' half of docs/ROSFOND-DATA-PATH.md section 3 and is Ben's decision, not a defect to fix unilaterally: with the dial off the model would report +0.081 drho/dvoid, 4x the only published whole-core measurement. Kept ON so the shipped physics stays inside a sourced envelope; flagged to_verify so it cannot be mistaken for derived.

coolant.derived_void.unit: core-average void fraction at nominal power
coolant.derived_void.source: COMPUTED, not guessed: channel energy balance from sourced plant data (docs/RBMK-PLANT-SYSTEMS.md, WP 83-89): 6 x 8000 m3/h at 750 kg/m3 = 10,000 kg/s; 3,200 MWt / 10,000 kg/s = 320 kJ/kg enthalpy rise; outlet steam quality 0.156 (matches the documented ~15%); void from quality with slip S=1.5. Replaces the fitted void = 0.05 + 0.08*(power-1), whose 0.05 was ~7x too low. To confirm against a measured RBMK channel void/quality distribution.

coolant.slip_ratio.source: Slip ratio S in alpha = 1/(1+((1-x)/x)(rho_v/rho_l)S). S=1 is homogeneous; real channel flow gives 1.2-2.0. 1.5 is representative. The one number in the coolant path not taken straight from a source.

coolant.axial_coupled_void.unit: core-average void fraction at nominal power, axial coupling on
coolant.axial_coupled_void.source: COMPUTED, not guessed: the same channel energy balance as coolant.derived_void, but marched up the flux shape the neutronics actually produces (bottom-peaked) rather than a cosine fallback. The bottom-peaked shape deposits more heat low in the channel, so the mean void is higher than the cosine-shape value (0.355). The reference critical state is seeded at this self-consistent fixed point (UnifiedReactorCore.selfConsistentVoid), which is what stops the old nominal drift.
coolant.axial_coupled_void.measured: 0.6364 mean void; core holds nominal power at 0.0% drift over 30 s

xsec.void_worth_axial.unit: dk/k per unit void (whole core, full axial profile)
xsec.void_worth_axial.source: Measured: the whole-core void worth with the void applied per axial node (+0.0248) vs as a core average (+0.0222) - only 12% higher, NOT the 'double' an earlier note claimed. Recorded to correct that note; the axial coupling is now the default.

xenon.macro_abs.unit: cm^-1 (added to the fuel cell thermal absorption per unit xenon ratio)
xenon.macro_abs.source: DERIVED, not fitted: sigma_Xe * N_Xe_eq. sigma_Xe = 2.65e-18 cm^2 (Xenon.SIGMA_XE); N_Xe_eq = (gamma_I + gamma_Xe) * Sigma_f * phi / (lambda_Xe + sigma_Xe * phi) with gamma_I=0.0639, gamma_Xe=0.00237, lambda_Xe=2.093e-5 /s, phi = Xenon.FLUX_FULL = 3e13 n/cm^2/s, Sigma_f ~ 2.56e-3 cm^-1. Gives N_Xe_eq ~ 5.07e13 cm^-3 and macro absorption ~1.34e-4 cm^-1. The one to-verify input is the reference flux (Xenon.FLUX_FULL). Replaces the fitted readout terms (0.024 in the lumped cores, -0.03 in Xenon.worth): xenon now acts through the neutron BALANCE. Measured worth: a 3x xenon ratio moves k_eff by -0.0227.
xenon.macro_abs.measured: -0.0227 dk/k for a 3x xenon ratio (about -0.011 at 2x), consistent with the ~3% real RBMK xenon worth

xsec.graphite_temp_derived.source: Derived from the OpenMC lattice cell: openmc/rbmk_graphite_mgxs.py sweeps the graphite temperature over 600-800 K (the range the S(alpha,beta) tables cover) and reports the fractional change of each homogenised 2-group constant per kelvin. Net cell coefficient +1.17e-5 /degC, POSITIVE. Consumed by RbmkGraphiteTemp, which scales the homogenised cell constants. Gated to the matching lattice table: it applies only when rbmk_lattice.json is the OpenMC table, because the slopes are fractional changes of THAT table's constants and flip sign against the 1-D table (whose fast-removal/up-scatter constants differ by an order of magnitude).
xsec.graphite_temp_derived.note: SIGN is sourced (INSAG-7 Table II-I, NUREG-1250: the RBMK's graphite coefficient is positive). MAGNITUDE is to_verify: a chord slope over 600-800 K extrapolated ~73 K to the 873 K operating point, and the ss21/ss12 slopes are nonlinear, so it overestimates the effect at operating temperature. Whole-core value of record is feedback.graphite_coeff (+6e-5, INSAG-7).
xsec.graphite_temp_derived.quote: Graphite temperature coefficient of reactivity ac (CC~') 6 x 10~5

fuel.max_temp.unit: degC (maximum fuel temperature at nominal power)
fuel.max_temp.source: docs/RBMK-PLANT-SYSTEMS.md, 'Maximum fuel temp | 600 C | WP 57' (WP = the plant technical description, cited per row). To confirm against a fetchable primary document (the WP itself, or an INSAG-7/NUREG figure) before promoting to verified. This is the value the fuel-temperature model is anchored to: FuelTemperature.anchoredToPeak fixes the effective fuel-to-coolant conduction rise so the model's hottest node reaches this documented maximum at nominal power.
fuel.max_temp.note: Replaces the fitted scalar NOMINAL_FUEL_C=640 and its FUEL_PER_POWER=600 line T=640+600*(P-1), neither registered. The old 640 was ~7% above the documented maximum; the anchor now IS the documented maximum, applied at the peak node, so the mean is lower (the fuel is hot only where the flux is).

fuel.rise_anchored.unit: K per (W/m) of per-rod linear power
fuel.rise_anchored.source: COMPUTED, not guessed: FuelTemperature.anchoredToPeak = (fuel.max_temp - peak coolant C) / peak per-rod linear power, evaluated at the self-consistent nominal state (UnifiedReactorCore.selfConsistentSeed). At nominal the hot node carries ~45.5 kW/m per rod and its coolant is ~267 C, giving R = (600-267)/45.5e3 ~= 7.3e-3 K/(W/m).
fuel.rise_anchored.note: This is an EFFECTIVE resistance, smaller than the physical UO2+gap+clad+film chain (~0.022 K/(W/m) volume-average), because the model's axial peaking factor is far higher than a real core's (see spatial.axial_peaking). It is anchored to the one sourced temperature so the peak is right; it must be re-derived from the physical chain once the axial shape is corrected. Consumed by UnifiedReactorCore.fuelConduction.

feedback.fuel_heat_capacity.source: The fuel time constant that was implicit in the old scalar model (UnifiedReactorCore.TAU_FUEL). Now registered so it is no longer an unregistered number.
feedback.fuel_heat_capacity.note: Source the fuel heat capacity (UO2 cp x fuel mass 192 t, docs/RBMK-PLANT-SYSTEMS.md WP 62) and the fuel-to-coolant conductance to derive this rather than carry a reference value. The DOF are the fuel mass and cp; both are sourced or sourceable.

rod.cartogram.quote: The SVG contains exactly 1,884 <rect> elements with fills #a5b5a4 x1661, #0067ce x127, #fed801 x24, #de1a03 x24, #555555 x24, #01b151 x12, #5f695f x12.
rod.cartogram.note: Replaces the previous placeholder radial-band cartogram in RodType.cartogram().

rod.lengths.quote: AZ 7,247 m; PK-AZ 6,772 m; AR 7,035 m; USP 4,088 m; RR 6,772 m (Tschernobyl 4 column).
rod.lengths.note: Replaces the single uniform ROD_ABSORBER_M = CORE_HEIGHT_M.

rod.displacer_lengths.quote: PK-AZ 4,560 m; AR 4,510 m; USP 6,700 m; RR 4,560 m; AZ N/A (no displacer).

rod.travel.quote: AZ Einfahrzeit 6 bis 7 s, Einfallzeit 2,5 s; PK-AZ/AR/RR Einfahrzeit 17 bis 18 s, Einfallzeit 12 s.
rod.travel.note: CONFLICT, recorded not resolved. The panel (SUZ-PANEL-TABLE) gives 17-18 s insertion for PK-AZ/AR/RR and 6-7 s for AZ; INSAG-7 p.51 states 'The time of insertion into the core was the same for all the RCPS rods (18-21 s)'. Two sources disagree on BOTH the absolute time and whether AZ rods are faster. The model uses 17.5 s (panel midpoint, = 0.4 m/s over the 7 m core height), which sits just below the INSAG-7 band. See rod.insert_s_insag7.

rod.worth_group.quote: AZ: -2 beta / N/A. PK-AZ: ? beta / +0,5 beta. AR: ? beta / +0,5 beta. RR: ? beta / +0,5 beta.
rod.worth_group.note: The table gives the ABSORBER worth as '?' for four of five types and only the DISPLACER worth (+0.5 beta) explicitly. The AZ group total of -2 beta is the one absorber figure given, and is used here to calibrate the rod-worth scale. The '?' values are NOT filled in by guesswork.

orm.reference.unit: equivalent manual rods (the regulation counts rods, not dk/k)
orm.reference.source: ТЕХНОЛОГИЧЕСКИЙ РЕГЛАМЕНТ 1Э-С-II (1983), ГЛАВА 9, §9.0 — the plant's own operating regulation, signed by B r y u k h a n o v / F o m i n / D y a t l o v / L y u t o v / G e l l e r m a n. Held in the repo at docs/primary-sources/reglament-1E-S-II-1983.txt
orm.reference.quote: «На номинальной мощности в стационарном режиме величина оперативного запаса реактивности должна составлять не менее 26÷30 стержней. Работа реактора при запасе менее 26 стержней допускается с разрешения главного инженера станции. При снижении оперативного запаса реактивности до 15 стержней реактор должен быть немедленно заглушен.» (ГЛАВА 9, lines 1939-1944). Also ГЛАВА 6 §6.6.4 and ГЛАВА 7 §7.1: during a power raise the margin must not fall below 15 rods.
orm.reference.note: PRIMARY SOURCE, and it supersedes the earlier value. This entry previously carried nominal 45-48 / warning 43 / limit 30 marked 'verified' from a YouTube SKALA simulator walkthrough (1JSP_gVXZTs), with this regulation demoted to a footnote. That was backwards: the walkthrough is a game, the regulation is the document the plant ran on and Dyatlov signed. The regulation's numbers are now the authority. The walkthrough's 45-48 is not necessarily wrong — it may describe a different unit or a later revision — but it cannot outrank the primary text, and the 43 'warning' setpoint has NO basis in the regulation at all, so it is dropped. CONSEQUENCE: the ORM alarm in RodBank must be re-derived from these numbers (26/30 nominal band, 15 shutdown), not from 45/43/30.

rod.pk_rr_positions.value: unresolved (12 rods inside the panel's 127-rod blue category)
rod.pk_rr_positions.quote: The panel draws 127 manual rods in one fill (#0067ce); the regulation splits them into РР 103 + ПК-РР 12 + ЛАР 12.
rod.pk_rr_positions.note: The cartogram can place 24 ПК-АЗ (they have their own fill) but not the 12 ПК-РР, and not the 12 ЛАР. Both are carried in the model as sub-populations with the correct counts and the correct per-type geometry, but their individual channel positions are NOT guessed. Resolving this needs the plant's техническое описание or a SUZ panel photo with the sub-types distinguishable.

xsec.control_hole_fraction.unit: fraction of the 250 mm lattice cell
xsec.control_hole_fraction.source: Channel geometry, not a fit: a control channel is a 114 mm bore in a 250 mm-pitch graphite cell (RbmkGeometry.CHANNEL_HOLE_M / LATTICE_PITCH_M), so the hole is (pi/4)*114^2/250^2 = 16.331% of the cell area and the graphite outside it is the other 83.669%.
xsec.control_hole_fraction.note: This is the BORE fraction - an UPPER BOUND on how much of the cell any rod can occupy, NOT the rod fraction. The rod itself is Ø70 mm (DOE Table G-2), only 6.16% of the cell; the remaining 10.17% of the cell inside the bore is water in the annular gap. See xsec.control_cell_split for the three-region split actually used. History: this entry replaced a hand-set 0.75/0.25 graphite/rod split that implied a Ø141 mm rod in a Ø114 mm hole (1.24x the bore, impossible, 53% overstatement); treating the bore AS the rod then replaced that, but was itself 2.65x too strong. The 114 mm bore and 250 mm pitch are still sourced only to EN Wikipedia and want a NIKIET/drawing confirmation.

rod.diameters.source: DOE/NE-0076 (Nov 1986), Appendix G, Table G-2 'Control Rod Specifications', PDF p. 177
rod.diameters.quote: Outer B4C Diameter 6.5 cm; Inner B4C Diameter 5.75 cm; Outer Clad Diameter 7.0 cm; Outer Clad Thickness 0.2 cm; Inner Clad Diameter 5.0 cm; Inner Clad Thickness 0.2 cm; Absorber Length/Section 98.4 cm; Total Length/Section 102.4 cm; Absorber Density 1.65 gm/CC; Displacer Clad Diameter 7.4 cm; Clad Thickness 0.25 cm.
rod.diameters.note: WESTERN SOURCE — REPLACEABLE, and only PARTLY corroborated. What survives: the DIAMETERS. Table G-2 is internally consistent as an annulus (B4C 65 mm OD / 57.5 mm ID inside a 70 mm clad, 50 mm bore cooling passage) and all three rod envelopes (Ø70 absorber, Ø74 displacer, 79 mm post-Chernobyl KRO sleeve) fit the 114 mm channel bore, so the diameter set is mutually consistent and physically coherent. What does NOT survive: the LENGTHS. The same page says the rod is five absorber sections of 102.4 cm = 5.12 m total with a 5 x 1 m = 5.0 m displacer, but the Russian panel table gives RR/PK-AZ 6.772 m absorber and 4.56 m displacer. That is a 24 % disagreement on absorber length and 10 % on displacer. The DOE report describes an earlier or different rod build, so its lengths must NOT be adopted; the panel lengths stay authoritative. Only the diameters are used from this source, because no Russian source for them has been obtained yet. Recorded in rod.length_conflict.

xsec.control_cell_split.unit: volume fraction of the 250 mm lattice cell
xsec.control_cell_split.source: Derived: DOE/NE-0076 Table G-2 rod diameters (Ø70 mm absorber, Ø74 mm displacer) inside the 114 mm channel bore of the 250 mm lattice cell
xsec.control_cell_split.quote: Outer Clad Diameter 7.0 cm ... Displacer Clad Diameter 7.4 cm (DOE/NE-0076 Table G-2); bore 114 mm and pitch 250 mm from RbmkGeometry.
xsec.control_cell_split.note: The ROBUST part: the rod is much smaller than the bore it sits in, so water fills the annular gap and the old model's 'rod = whole bore' was wrong by a large factor. Every candidate diameter (65-80 mm) is far below the 114 mm bore, so the DIRECTION of this correction does not depend on which source is right. The UNCERTAIN part: the exact fractions follow the DOE diameters, which are to_verify (no Russian source yet). If the true absorber OD were 80 mm the absorber fraction would be 0.0804 rather than 0.0616 - a 30 % difference in rod strength. So the magnitude stays flagged until a Russian drawing fixes the diameter. The 2.65x figure quoted above is DOE-specific.

rod.density.source: CONFLICT: DOE/NE-0076 Table G-2 'Absorber Density 1.65 gm/CC' vs the 2.52 g/cm3 used by tools/lattice/emit_constants.py
rod.density.note: MEASURED SENSITIVITY, not a guess: B4C density enters the two-group constants linearly, so 1.65 vs 2.52 is a 1.53x swing in absorber strength - a far bigger lever than the rod diameter (1.2x). Run through ExperimentVariantsSelfTest at the MODELLED scram rate, 1.65 gives +187.1% and 2.52 gives +188.0% on the 26 April excursion: 0.9 percentage points. So the density conflict is real but it is NOT what decides the accident - the rod axial geometry is. WHY THE TWO NUMBERS DIFFER: 2.52 g/cm3 is the THEORETICAL CRYSTAL density of B4C, i.e. 100% dense with zero porosity; 1.65 is 65.5% of theoretical, which is a plausible hot-pressed pellet density. So they are probably not a contradiction at all but the same material quoted dense vs as-fabricated, and the physically correct one for a real pellet is the LOWER figure. That also kills the earlier '1.65 may be a typo for 2.65' idea: 2.65 g/cm3 is 105% of the crystal density, which is impossible for B4C. The model currently uses 2.52, i.e. it assumes a fully dense absorber and therefore OVERSTATES rod worth by up to 1.53x. Switching to 1.65 would be the physically better default, but it should be done together with the diameter question, not piecemeal.

rod.insert_s_insag7.source: INSAG-7, The Chernobyl Accident: Updating of INSAG-1, p. 51 (section on the fast-response EPS)
rod.insert_s_insag7.quote: The time of insertion into the core was the same for all the RCPS rods (18-21 s). This means that their division into functional groups of emergency protection rods and manual control rods was a notional one. ... no studies were carried out to determine the required speed of response of the EPS rods in order that the time of core insertion be less than 18s.
rod.insert_s_insag7.note: WESTERN/IAEA source, contradicts the panel table in rod.travel on both the time (18-21 vs 17-18 s) and the AZ exception (INSAG-7 says uniform, the panel says AZ is 6-7 s). The 0.4 m/s drive rate is stated three times in INSAG-7 (p.51, p.93, p.113) and is consistent with the panel's 17-18 s over a ~7 m stroke, so the SPEED is agreed even though the TIMES are not. The 18-21 s figure likely includes the slower final seating phase after the 0.4 m/s run. Unresolved; needs a Russian primary source for the insertion-time curve.

rod.length_conflict.source: CONFLICT: DOE/NE-0076 Appendix G p.G-1 and Table G-2 vs SUZ-PANEL-TABLE
rod.length_conflict.quote: The RR, AR, LAR, and AZ rods are assembled from five absorbing sections for a total length of 5.12 meters. The USP rods are assembled from three absorbing sections and have a total length of 3.05 meters. ... The displacer is made up of five, one meter long cylindrical sections (DOE/NE-0076 p.G-1).
rod.length_conflict.note: DOE 5 x 102.4 cm = 5.12 m absorber and 5 x 1 m displacer contradict the panel's 6.772 m / 4.56 m. Both cannot describe the same rod. The DOE text also says the USP is 3.05 m where the panel says 4.088 m, and that all rods except USP drive from the top. The repo uses the panel lengths (Russian source, preferred) and takes ONLY the diameters from DOE. This conflict is the reason rod.diameters is to_verify, not verified: the diameter figures have no independent Russian confirmation yet.

rod.openmc_model_geometry.source: openmc/control_rod_test.py, channel_universe(): rod_r defaults to 2.5 cm, rodclad = rod_r + 0.4
rod.openmc_model_geometry.note: The OpenMC model already treats the rod as a THIN absorber in a water-filled bore rather than a plug - the same correction just made in the Java control cell - so the two now agree in structure. But its radius is wrong: rod_r=2.5 cm is the 50 mm INNER CLAD bore, not the absorber. Per DOE Table G-2 the B4C is a 65 mm OD / 57.5 mm ID annulus (r 2.875-3.25 cm) and the outer clad is 70 mm (r 3.5 cm). The model's 'b4c' cylinder therefore sits in the cooling passage and its 'clad' shell at 2.9 cm is inside where the real B4C starts. Not yet fixed: the script has not been re-run against the corrected radii, so any control-rod result it produced so far describes a Ø50 mm solid absorber, which is physically not the RBMK rod.

test.scram_rate.source: RbmkGeometry.ROD_INSERTION_PER_S = 1 / ROD_FULL_TRAVEL_S (17.5 s, panel table); the test now reads that constant -- INTERNAL code fact, not an external citation: needs a primary source for the 17.5 s stroke before it can be marked verified.
test.scram_rate.note: BUG FIXED. ExperimentVariantsSelfTest hardcoded 0.2 insertion/s - a 5 s full stroke - while the model's own constant is 0.057/s (17.5 s). The test was therefore measuring a scram 3.5x faster than the plant can perform, and understating the accident. At the real rate the 26 April excursion is +188%, not +35%. The direction was never wrong, only the magnitude. Any earlier figure quoting ~35% is from the wrong rate. STATUS: to_verify because the gate requires an external URL + verbatim quote for 'verified', and this is a code-consistency fact.

test.power_units.value: arbitrary units, normalised to the reference state = 1.0
test.power_units.source: RbmkTransientSolver.power() javadoc: 'Mean fission source over the active nodes - the reactor power (arbitrary units)' -- INTERNAL code fact, not an external citation: needs a primary source for the 17.5 s stroke before it can be marked verified.
test.power_units.note: The accident test's assertion text used to say 'x nominal', which is wrong: the reference state is 1.0 and the 26 April variant is SEEDED at 5.63 of those units. Those 5.63 are a property of the seeded low-power state, NOT a claim the reactor ran at 563% power. Ratios (peak/p0, end/p0) are meaningful; absolute power is not, and nothing in the model should be read as an absolute MW figure until a normalisation to nominal power is added. STATUS: to_verify because the gate requires an external URL + verbatim quote for 'verified', and this is a code-consistency fact.

xenon.flux_full.unit: n/cm^2/s (core-average thermal flux at nominal power)
xenon.flux_full.source: DERIVED from the shipped lattice table and geometry, not fitted: phi = P_fis / (E_f * Sigma_f * V), with P_fis = 3200 MWt (PlantPhysics.P_THERMAL_W), E_f = 200 MeV, Sigma_f = (nsf1+nsf2)/nu from rbmk_lattice.json (0.00286 /cm, cell-homogenised), V = 1661 * 0.25^2 * 7.28 = 756 m3 (the homogenised core). Gives 4.62e13 n/cm^2/s. Consistency: the same inputs give 4.23 kW/litre, in the RBMK's documented 4-5 kW/litre band, so the normalisation is self-consistent.
xenon.flux_full.note: REPLACES the unsourced Xenon.FLUX_FULL = 3.0e13. That value is 1.54x low. It matters: at 3.0e13 the xenon pit peaks 1.91x equilibrium at 8.5 h; at 4.62e13 it peaks 2.41x at 8.8 h, a 26 % deeper pit. The pit is what forced the operators to withdraw rods into the ORM violation, so this is on the accident path. Still to_verify because E_f=200 MeV and nu=2.43 are textbook, not from a NIKIET source; the sensitivity to both is weak (phi ~ 1/(E_f*nu)), but they must be pinned.

orm.burnup_balance.unit: pcm and equivalent manual rods, k_eff including bare-cylinder leakage
orm.burnup_balance.source: COMPUTED by tools/lattice/burnup.py (report()) against the repo's own 69-group solver and ENDF/B-VIII.0 cache; guarded by tools/lattice/test_burnup.py (14 checks). Fuel depletion U-235 -> Pu-239/240/241 with Bondarenko-shielded capture; lumped FP 50 b 1/v (Lamarsh Table 3.2); equilibrium Xe-135 and Sm-149; leakage from bare-cylinder B^2 at 11.8 m x 7.0 m with the cell's own migration area.
orm.burnup_balance.note: BURNUP DOES MOST OF THE WORK, AND IS NOT THE WHOLE STORY. Fresh fuel carries +21359 pcm of k_eff excess (394 rods); at 10.3 MWd/kg with FP and equilibrium poisons it is +6500 pcm (120 rods). So depletion closes about 70% of the gap the orm.scale_calibration note describes (202 rods held in the rods at the model's critical point). It does NOT reach 26-30 rods: 120 rods is still 4x the regulation band. Two candidate explanations were tested and REJECTED quantitatively, not waved away: (a) fission products cannot close it - reaching 26-30 rods needs a lumped sigma_c of about 360 b, seven times the textbook 50 b, and (b) the 211 control channels sitting as water columns cost only about 650 pcm. CONSEQUENCE: do not seed an arbitrary FP inventory to force ORM to 26-30; that would fit the answer. The residual gap is most likely the lattice's fresh-fuel k_inf being too high (1.34442 vs the ~1.29 in the shipped table) and the absence of any in-core burnup distribution - unit 4's 10.3 MWd/kg is a core AVERAGE, and the regulation margin is set by the least-burned channels. Modelling a burnup DISTRIBUTION, not a single average, is the next step.
orm.burnup_balance.history: Supersedes the qualitative claim in orm.scale_calibration that the gap is 'exactly the burnup/fission-product reactivity'. That direction is right; the magnitude is not - burnup explains ~70%, not 100%.

burnup.target_mwd_per_kg.unit: MWd/kg U (core-average discharge burnup at the accident)
burnup.target_mwd_per_kg.source: Carried from the earlier session's reading of INSAG-7 for unit 4; NOT yet re-pinned to a page/quote in this repo.
burnup.target_mwd_per_kg.note: NEEDS A PRIMARY CITATION before it is load-bearing. The sensitivity is real: burnup sets the whole reactivity balance above. What IS verified independently is the BURNUP RATE, 0.0167 MWd/kg/day, derived from 3200 MWt over 192 t of uranium at 9.173 g/cm3 - and the cross-check that 3 full-power years at that rate gives 18.3 MWd/kg, in the RBMK's documented ~20 MWd/kg discharge range. If 10.3 is wrong, re-run burnup.py at the right value; the tool takes it as a parameter.

orm.scale_calibration.unit: rods (model ORM at a plausible operating point, ~31% insertion)
orm.scale_calibration.source: MEASURED from OrmSelfTest against the shipped cartogram; the regulation target is ГЛАВА 9 of 1Э-С-II (26-30 rods).
orm.scale_calibration.note: ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-11-18 (supersedes the 'rod-worth scale is 1.6x high' guess below). It is NOT a rod-worth calibration error and must NOT be 'fixed' by retuning the rod-worth scale: that scale is anchored to a sourced figure (24 AZ rods = 2 beta_eff -> one manual rod = 0.000536 dk/k, provenance rod.worth_group) and agrees with the anchor. The defect is MISSING PHYSICS: the lattice table is FRESH fuel (k_inf = 1.2893), and RbmkTransientSolver has no burnup and no fission-product inventory, so it forces the reference state critical by rescaling the fission source (nsfScale = 1/k) at a hand-chosen NOMINAL_INSERTION = 0.80. A fresh core therefore needs ~29% dk/k of rod worth to be subcritical, where the regulation's 26-30 rods is only 1.4-1.6% dk/k. Measured at the model's own critical point: ORM = 202 rods = 10.8% dk/k held in the rods. The gap (10.8% - 1.5% = ~9.3% dk/k) is exactly the burnup/fission-product reactivity a real equilibrium core has already spent. CONSEQUENCE: ORM in-game is not comparable to the regulation until burnup is modelled; the 26/15 LIMITS are correct and stay. FIX = model burnup (or seed an equilibrium fission-product inventory), not a retune. The 45-48 figure from the SKALA walkthrough is also consistent with a low-burnup core, which is why the model matched the video and not the regulation.

trip.az1_az5_setpoints.unit: mixed, as the regulation states them (see quote)
trip.az1_az5_setpoints.source: ТЕХНОЛОГИЧЕСКИЙ РЕГЛАМЕНТ 1Э-С-II (1983), ГЛАВА 3 «ПЕРЕЧЕНЬ АВАРИЙНЫХ ЗАЩИТ РЕАКТОРА», items АЗ-1 .. АЗ-5. Repo: docs/primary-sources/reglament-1E-S-II-1983.txt lines 977-1046
trip.az1_az5_setpoints.quote: АЗ-1: «снижение расхода питательной воды до 0,75 текущего»; «снижение расхода воды в КМПЦ … через любой из 3-х ГЦН … до 5000 м3/ч». АЗ-5: «уменьшение периода разгона до 10±2 сек при мощности … до 160 мВт(т) … и до 20 сек в остальном диапазоне»; «повышение уровня мощности на 0,5% Nном … при мощности до 160 Мвт(т)»; «повышение уровня мощности на 10% Nном над заданным при мощности 160÷3200 мВт(т)»; «повышение давления в реакторном пространстве до аварийной уставки – 0,15 кгс/см2»; «повышение давления в барабан-сепараторах до 75 кгс/см2 (абсолютного)»; «снижение уровней в барабан-сепараторах … до величины -1100 мм»; «повышение уровней … до +250 мм»; «снижение расхода воды в напорный коллектор СУЗ до аварийной уставки (800 м3/ч)».
trip.az1_az5_setpoints.note: These are the PROTECTION SETPOINTS, from the plant's own regulation, so they replace the earlier 'setpoint to be read from the regulation' placeholders. Note the regulation has NO single '104% overpower' number: the power protection is a MARGIN over the setpoint (10% Nnom over the заданный level in the 5-100% range, 0.5% below 5%), plus a period (rate) protection at 20 s. So a '104% trip' was the wrong shape; the real protection is a rate trip and a margin trip. IMPLEMENTATION GAP: PlantSystem.checkTrips currently trips feedwater at 0.1 of nominal, not at the regulation's 0.75 of CURRENT flow, and implements none of the period, power-margin, pressure or separator-pressure trips.
